text:
Mike Cheng: Heads-up — Acme private deployment asking for 'air-gapped-like' isolation. Two quick asks: (1) network policy template to prevent unintended DB egress from app nodes, (2) how do we scope KMS keys for on-prem so operator/admin consoles can't decrypt customer secrets? :lock:
Sara K: +1 on both. For network policy we usually do default-deny ns + explicit allow to svc accounts. Simple example below (apply to app namespace):

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-unless-specific
spec:
  podSelector: {} # applies to all pods in ns
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: datastore
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          infra: shared-services
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
        except: [10.0.3.0/24] # allow internal cluster subnets as needed
```

Sarah: That blocks outbound to anything not explicitly allowed. Add hostNetwork exceptions if using node-exporter etc. :white_check_mark:
Jamal Ortiz: KMS scoping — for private/on-prem we recommend a split-control model: customer-managed CMKs (HSM/KMS) that only the runtime process can use via short-lived mTLS certs. Operators get audit-only access. Key points:
- Use envelope encryption: runtime talks to local KMS, operator never has plaintext.
- KMS auth via service identity tied to workload (SPIFFE) and hardware attestation where available.
- Audit logs forwarded to customer-owned SIEM; redact operator metadata.

Tanya Ops: For the Acme checklist, add these deployment steps:
- Ensure default-deny egress for all non-infra namespaces
- Block hostPath mounts for app tanks
- Disable kubernetes API server anonymous auth + lock down kubelet read-only port
- KMS key rotation policy: 90 days and automated via rotation job (customer can opt longer)

Mike Cheng: Nice. One follow-up: how do we handle operator EMERGENCY access (e.g., decrypt for forensics) without breaking separation?
LiaSecurityBot: Alert: policy request created #PR-1298 by Mike Cheng (1845123456) — link: https://tickets.internal/PR-1298
Jamal Ortiz: Recommended pattern: break-glass requires multi-party approval + ephemeral session with audit video + key usage logged to immutable store. Implement via an access gateway that issues one-time unwrap tokens that are scoped and time-limited. Example flow:
1) Operator requests via portal (requires 2 approvers)
2) Gateway mints one-time KMS unwrap token scoped to ciphertext id
3) Runtime performs unwrap, writes to ephemeral location with TTL, fetchable only by approved investigator
4) All steps logged to customer-owned audit backend

Sara K: Also flag: we found a container-runtime vuln pattern (privilege escalation via CAP_SYS_ADMIN in init containers) in a customer triage last month. For private deployments add an admission controller policy to deny CAP_SYS_ADMIN and hostPID unless explicitly approved.
Mike Cheng: OK, I'll post the checklist to Acme and attach the NP + KMS flow doc. Who wants to review before I send? :eyes:
Tanya Ops: I can review — will check rotation + playbook entries.
Sara K: I can review the KMS flow and audit hooks.
Mike Cheng: Great — aiming to send by EOD PST. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
